comparisons.coverage_method: Verified the complete manifest (135 exact local_path entries) against selectors libero/libero/bddl_files/*.bddl, libero/libero/benchmark/*.py, and libero/libero/envs/predicates/*.py. Enumerated the original BDDL inventory, checked libero_suite_task_map.py, searched all selected originals for rail/bearing/ball/jig/carriage/slide/align/insert/transfer/mount/block/track/drawer mechanisms, and read the closest BDDL and Open predicate implementation completely.
comparisons.objective: The candidate transfers a detachable, uncaged recirculating-ball LM block from a rail onto a physically butted jig. LIBERO's closest task only opens a cabinet drawer.
comparisons.physical_skill: Both involve constrained linear motion, but LIBERO tests pulling a captive articulated drawer. It does not test bimanual end-face mating, maintaining parallel continuous support across two bodies, regrasping during transfer, or retaining freely simulated rolling elements.
comparisons.success_condition: The candidate requires complete rail-to-jig transfer with physical interface contact and every ball retained, plus no gap, jam, contamination, impact, or unsafe inclination. LIBERO requires only the drawer region's Open state; Open delegates to arg.is_open().

closest_tasks.name: Open the middle drawer of the cabinet
closest_tasks.objective: Open the middle drawer of a wooden cabinet.
closest_tasks.physical_skill: Pull a captive prismatic drawer along its existing guide.
closest_tasks.reason: The shared linear sliding primitive is insufficient overlap. The LIBERO object remains captive and there is no transfer across a separately aligned interface or rolling-element preservation outcome.

comparisons.reason: The complete selected LIBERO corpus contains drawer motion and ordinary placement but no task whose central tested ability is continuous-support transfer of an uncaged bearing block while preserving loose circulating elements.

comparisons.coverage_method: Verified the complete manifest (381 exact local_path entries) against robocasa/environments/kitchen/*.py, robocasa/environments/__init__.py, and robocasa/utils/dataset_registry.py. Enumerated every selected original, reviewed registry-visible task classes, searched the full inventory for the candidate's mechanism, and completely read the closest rack-placement and captive-rack sliding implementations, including their success checks.
comparisons.objective: The candidate removes an LM block from one support and transfers it onto a separately held jig without exposing unsupported ball rows. RoboCasa's closest tasks either slide a captive dishwasher rack or place food containers onto fixed appliance racks.
comparisons.physical_skill: SlideDishwasherRack shares guided translation, while rack-placement tasks share placement onto a support. Neither combines bimanual flush end-face alignment, continuous cross-interface support, force-limited bearing-block translation, alignment-preserving regrasping, and containment of free rolling elements.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate success requires complete transfer, physical end-face contact, parallel axes, all balls retained, safe release, and absence of gap, jam, contamination, impact, or inclination. SlideDishwasherRack checks only normalized rack position; ToastOnCorrectRack checks rack contact and gripper distance.

closest_tasks.name: SlideDishwasherRack
closest_tasks.quote: ep_meta["lang"] = f"Fully slide the top dishwasher rack {direction}."
closest_tasks.objective: Fully slide the top dishwasher rack in or out.
closest_tasks.physical_skill: Translate a captive rack along its installed guide.
closest_tasks.success_condition: For pulling, current_pos >= 0.95; for pushing, current_pos <= 0.05.
closest_tasks.reason: This is the strongest guided-sliding neighbor, but it does not transfer a carriage between independently aligned supports or test loss of internal rolling elements.

closest_tasks.name: ToastOnCorrectRack
closest_tasks.objective: Open a toaster oven and place bread and meat on specified fixed racks.
closest_tasks.physical_skill: Pick and place objects onto selected supports in an appliance.
closest_tasks.success_condition: Both objects contact their assigned racks and the gripper is far from them.
closest_tasks.reason: Rack contact is ordinary placement, not a continuous-support handoff of a recirculating carriage with a no-loss constraint.

comparisons.reason: RoboCasa contains captive guided motion and rack placement, but no original task tests the candidate's combined support-interface construction and rolling-element-containment ability.

comparisons.coverage_method: Verified all 11 manifest local_path entries against simpler_env/__init__.py, env_builder.py, and every selected ManiSkill2_real2sim env file. Read the registration sources and the complete closest articulated-drawer implementations, including reset and evaluate logic.
comparisons.objective: The candidate transfers a detachable bearing block between a service rail and mating jig. SimplerEnv's closest registered family opens or closes a cabinet drawer, optionally placing an object in it.
comparisons.physical_skill: SimplerEnv tests manipulation of one captive drawer joint and generic placement. It does not require a second hand to butt and stabilize a jig, bridge two guide surfaces, preserve parallelism during regrasping, or contain free balls.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate success includes complete block transfer and retention of every ball with damage and unsafe-motion exclusions. OpenDrawer succeeds from one joint coordinate threshold; PlaceIntoClosedDrawer additionally requires a staged flag and at least one object-drawer contact.

closest_tasks.physical_skill: Pull a captive articulated drawer against joint friction.
closest_tasks.success_condition: The target drawer joint position is at least 0.15.
closest_tasks.reason: The task shares guided linear motion only. It has no detachable carriage, support handoff, bimanual interface alignment, or loose-element loss mode.

closest_tasks.reason: Contact with a receptacle does not test continuous bearing-race support or preservation of circulating elements during a rail-to-jig transfer.

comparisons.reason: The complete SimplerEnv inventory is small and fully resolved; its closest mechanisms are captive drawer articulation and generic placement, not the candidate's central ability.

comparisons.coverage_method: Verified the complete manifest (1,122 exact local_path entries) against both recorded BDDL activity-definition selectors and the selected task/state backend files. Enumerated both complete activity inventories, searched all originals for bearing, rail, installation, attachment, transfer, and repair neighbors, read the closest BDDL definitions completely, and read all 573 lines of attached_to.py to resolve the abstract attached predicate's actual mechanism.
comparisons.objective: The candidate performs a reversible service transfer of an uncaged recirculating-ball block onto a physically butted jig. BEHAVIOR's closest bearing-named task cleans attached skateboard wheels, while its closest installation task attaches a hitch to a pickup.
comparisons.physical_skill: Cleaning skateboard bearings is represented as removing grease coverage, not bearing removal or element handling. Trailer-hitch installation uses proximity/orientation meta-links and backend attachment creation; it does not test sliding a carriage across a continuously supported interface while retaining free balls.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate success is based on measured support contact, parallelism, transfer completion, ball count/containment, damage exclusions, and stable release. The cleaning task only negates Covered; the hitch task requires Attached, whose backend aligns poses and creates a fixed or spherical joint after threshold checks.

closest_tasks.name: clean_skateboard_bearings-0
closest_tasks.objective: Clean grease from skateboard wheels described by the activity name as bearing cleaning.
closest_tasks.physical_skill: Remove a covering substance from attached wheels.
closest_tasks.success_condition: No skateboard wheel remains Covered by grease.
closest_tasks.reason: The bearing label does not encode removal, rail transfer, circulation, or rolling-element containment; the original goal is solely a coverage-state change.

closest_tasks.name: installing_a_trailer_hitch-0
closest_tasks.objective: Attach a trailer hitch to a pickup.
closest_tasks.physical_skill: Bring compatible attachment meta-links within position and orientation thresholds.
closest_tasks.success_condition: The hitch's AttachedTo parent is the pickup; the backend then creates a fixed or spherical joint.
closest_tasks.reason: This tests terminal attachment, and the backend explicitly pose-aligns the child before creating a joint. It does not model a contact-preserving rail handoff or free rolling-element retention.

comparisons.reason: Neither the bearing-named activity nor the resolved attachment implementation exercises the candidate's central continuous-support transfer ability. The backend inspection removes ambiguity that Attached might implicitly represent such a mechanism.

comparisons.coverage_method: Verified the single complete manifest entry and read published-task-definitions.txt in full. The original publication explicitly enumerates all 19 considered tasks, identifies the ten retained tasks, and describes their physical abstractions, allowing complete registry-level comparison without relying on the manifest as task evidence.
comparisons.objective: The candidate is an LM-guide service operation: align a removing/mounting jig to a rail and transfer an uncaged bearing block without ball loss. DataCenterBench's nearest retained task is moving a slider; its considered connection tasks cover plugs, clips, and keyed or fastened parts.
comparisons.physical_skill: Move a slider shares one-dimensional hand motion, but the publication says its tabletop dimmer copies only the sliding motion. It does not require bimanual alignment of separate supports, continuous bearing-race support, controlled carriage handoff, regrasping, or ball containment.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate success requires exact physical support continuity, completed transfer, all balls retained, safe inclination, no damage/contamination, and stable release. The published slider task tests moving a two-position control; no published task scores rolling-element preservation or rail-to-jig transfer.

closest_tasks.name: Move a slider
closest_tasks.quote: Real UPS mode selector has two fixed positions. Our dimmer copies only the sliding motion.
closest_tasks.objective: Move a tabletop slider standing in for a UPS mode selector.
closest_tasks.physical_skill: Single-axis actuation of a fixed control.
closest_tasks.success_condition: Move the control to the requested fixed position.
closest_tasks.reason: The source itself limits this task to copied sliding motion. The candidate's tested outcome depends on constructing and maintaining a continuous support path and preventing loss of independent bearing elements.

closest_tasks.name: Insert a battery the right way round
closest_tasks.quote: Real polarity-dependent step. Our AA holder stands in for the coin-cell holder.
closest_tasks.objective: Insert a battery with correct polarity; this task was considered but left out.
closest_tasks.physical_skill: Orient and insert one rigid item into a holder.
closest_tasks.success_condition: Battery is seated in the correct orientation.
closest_tasks.reason: This is insertion into a terminal receptacle, not a sliding handoff between aligned guide surfaces, and it has no continuous-support or element-containment outcome.

comparisons.reason: The publication's complete retained-and-considered list contains generic sliding and insertion but no task matching the candidate's central maintenance mechanism.

comparisons.coverage_method: Verified all 110 manifest local_path entries against task/RoboDojo/tasks/*.py, task/RoboDojo/config/*.yml, and task_registry.py. Enumerated every registered task/config, searched all originals for alignment, insertion, rack, ball, guided motion, and transfer mechanisms, and completely read both the task and configuration files for the strongest insertion and loose-ball neighbors.
comparisons.objective: The candidate transfers one recirculating bearing carriage between aligned support profiles while preserving all its balls. RoboDojo's closest tasks insert three separate tubes into a rack and pour seven balls from a cup into a vase.
comparisons.physical_skill: InsertTubes tests repeated axis alignment and depth insertion into terminal slots. PourBallsIntoVase tests bulk transfer of free spheres between containers. Neither requires bimanual butt alignment of two supports, sliding a carriage across their boundary, preserving a closed circulation path, or maintaining every ball inside that carriage during regrasping.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate success requires physical rail-jig contact and parallelism, complete carriage transfer, retention of every ball in four circulating rows, no gap/jam/damage, and stable release. InsertTubes checks depth, containment, upright orientation, and robot return; PourBalls checks each sphere inside the vase, cup upright, and robot return.

closest_tasks.name: insert_tubes
closest_tasks.quote: templates = ["Insert the three tubes into the rack one by one."]
closest_tasks.objective: Insert three test tubes into a rack one by one.
closest_tasks.physical_skill: Align separate elongated objects with receptacle slots and insert them to depth.
closest_tasks.success_condition: Each tube is inside the slot, reaches 0.045 depth, is upright within 30 degrees, and the robot returns to origin for the completion check.
closest_tasks.reason: This is a plausible precision-insertion neighbor, but it terminates each object in a receptacle and does not test a guide-to-guide handoff or preservation of independent internal elements.

closest_tasks.name: pour_balls_into_vase
closest_tasks.quote: templates = ["Pour all the balls from the cup into the vase."]
closest_tasks.objective: Pour seven free balls from a cup into a vase.
closest_tasks.physical_skill: Manipulate and tilt a container to transfer loose spheres in bulk.
closest_tasks.success_condition: All seven spheres are inside the vase, the cup is upright, and the robot returns to origin.
closest_tasks.reason: Both tasks make loss of free balls observable, but RoboDojo intentionally transfers the balls out of their original container. The candidate must keep balls contained within a moving recirculating block while its support changes; that is a different central ability and outcome.

comparisons.reason: RoboDojo separately covers precision insertion and loose-ball pouring, but no registered task combines them into continuous-support carriage transfer with no rolling-element loss.
